CBSE • CLASS 10 • MATHEMATICS

Ch 14 · Probability — Practice

Attempt first, then open the answer. Everything here is original practice material mapped to the current syllabus.

MCQs

The probability of an impossible event is: (a) 1 (b) 0 (c) 1/2 (d) undefined

(b) 0.

Two dice are thrown together. The total number of outcomes is: (a) 6 (b) 12 (c) 36 (d) 24

(c) 36.

The number of face cards in a deck of 52 cards is: (a) 8 (b) 12 (c) 16 (d) 4

(b) 12. Jacks, queens and kings of four suits.

Written questions

1 marks A card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck. What is the probability that it is a red king?

There are 2 red kings, so P = 2/52 = 1/26.

2 marks A die is thrown once. Find the probability of getting (i) a prime number, (ii) a number greater than 4.

Primes on a die are 2, 3, 5, so P = 3/6 = 1/2.
Numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6, so P = 2/6 = 1/3.

3 marks Two dice are thrown together. Find the probability that the sum is 9.

Total outcomes = 36.
Favourable pairs: (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3) — 4 outcomes.
P = 4/36 = 1/9.

2 marks A bag contains 5 red and 3 green balls. One ball is drawn at random. Find the probability that it is not red.

Total = 8. P(not red) = P(green) = 3/8.
Equivalently, 1 − 5/8 = 3/8.

3 marks A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck. Find the probability that it is (i) a face card, (ii) neither a king nor a red card.

(i) There are 12 face cards, so P = 12/52 = 3/13.
(ii) Red cards are 26, of which 2 are kings. Neither a king nor red means a black card that is not a king: 26 − 2 = 24.
P = 24/52 = 6/13.
